content_of_post_to_comment:
I recently quit my corporate job and have been struggling to maintain a consistent routine now that I no longer have external structure.

My biggest issue is waking up early. I have a hard time falling asleep early, and sometimes I sleep until 1 PM. I’ve tried multiple alarms, putting my alarm across the room, keeping my curtains open for morning light, and only using my bedroom for sleep or reading. Despite all of this, I still struggle to get myself up consistently.

When I was working, I had somewhere I needed to be, so getting up wasn’t really optional. Now that I’m responsible for creating my own schedule, I’m realizing how difficult it is to hold myself accountable.

The hardest part is that sleeping through half the day makes me feel extremely unproductive and disappointed in myself. Then I feel guilty, which makes it harder to get motivated and start the things I actually want to accomplish. I feel so horrible as a person and I can’t move forward

For anyone who’s dealt with this, what actually helped you become more disciplined and get into a routine? Especially when you don’t have a job or anyone else expecting you to be up at a certain time. I feel like I’ve tried all the basic advice, so I’d love to hear what actually worked for you.
comment: I went through something similar after leaving a structured job, and I realized I was trying to recreate an employer's pressure with alarms and rules. What helped was making one non-negotiable morning commitment outside my home, even something small like a walk or coffee run. The goal wasn't waking up early first; it was giving the day a reason to start.
